clue.text: Comedian keeping quiet in favour of Congreve's comedy Lady

indicators.note: a comedian keeping something holds it within, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a wit is a joker, a funny person
SH is the call for quiet
to be for something is to be in favour of it

explanation.surface: A comic hushes up while championing a lady from a Restoration comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Wishfort is the vain old widow in Congreve's The Way of the World.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Wishfort is a character in William Congreve's play The Way of the World.

clue.text: Court authoritarian, almost a toff

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of complete

parts.note: an authoritarian figure is stern

explanation.surface: A strict judge in court turns out to be something of an upper-class gent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter N from STERN, leaving STER. 'Toff' is British slang for a posh person; Bertie Wooster is P.G. Wodehouse's archetypal one.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertie Wooster, Wodehouse's idle aristocrat, is the literary model of an upper-class gentleman.

clue.text: Jottings about Spark's bachelor, Patrick

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: jottings are notes

explanation.surface: Somebody scribbles notes on a single man named Patrick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NOTES round. Patrick Seton is a fraudulent medium in Muriel Spark's novel The Bachelors.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrick Seton is one of the single men in Muriel Spark's novel The Bachelors.

clue.text: Upset, Echo provided a cry of disgust

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means knocked over, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: E is Echo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
provided that means if

explanation.surface: An agitated nymph, if upset, lets out a cry of disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns E plus IF, read bottom to top in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fie is an old exclamation expressing disgust or outrage.

clue.text: Maybe Caulfield and Stradlater returned low marks in classes

indicators.note: in means the reversed low and the mark sit inside the word for classes

parts.note: rates are classes or grades, as in first-rate

indicators.note: returned means the word for low is read backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Two schoolboys get poor grades back in their lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Holden Caulfield and Stradlater share a dormitory room in Salinger's The Catcher in the Rye; 'Maybe' marks them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Holden Caulfield and Stradlater share a room at Pencey Prep, making them examples of people who room together.

clue.text: Sexual activity husband follows in a book

indicators.note: follows means the husband comes after the sexual activity in the answer

parts.note: the rut is the mating season of deer and similar animals

explanation.surface: A spouse comes after a romp, as recorded in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: In Heartbreak House, Lady Ariadne's complete oath

parts.note: utter means complete, total
a word, as in word of honour, is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: In a Shaw play, an aristocratic lady swears a thorough vow.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Ariadne Utterword is Captain Shotover's daughter in Shaw's play Heartbreak House.

clue.text: Perhaps what The Entertainer did, keeping one uplifted

indicators.note: keeping means the larger word holds the smaller one inside it

parts.note: an entertainer may host a show, so he hosted
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Osborne's music-hall comic, Archie Rice, may have raised spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside HOSTED. The Entertainer is John Osborne's play about a music-hall comic; 'Perhaps' marks hosting as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hoisted has been raised up, as a flag is lifted up a pole.

clue.text: Presently the author is unknown

definitions.meaning: an old word for soon, shortly
the abbreviation for anonymous, written under a work whose writer is not known

explanation.definitionFit: Anon means soon in older English and abbreviates anonymous for a work without a named writer.

clue.text: Work of harbour to support fish

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: the bleak is a small freshwater fish
to house is to harbour or shelter

explanation.surface: A harbour structure stands beneath a fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer HOUSE written under BLEAK holds it up. The 'Work' is Dickens's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak House is a novel by Charles Dickens, a work of literature.

clue.text: Airing Richter's prize novel as a musical

parts.note: a programme that is airing is on
Conrad Richter's The Town won the Pulitzer Prize for fiction

explanation.surface: A broadcast of a prizewinning book adapted for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Town is a Bernstein, Comden and Green stage musical about three sailors on leave.

clue.text: Baroque composer's unfinished tale containing too much

indicators.note: containing means the shortened word holds the other piece inside
unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale can be a lie, a made-up story
OTT is over the top, too much

explanation.surface: An incomplete story about a composer is overdone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay; 'unfinished' drops the last letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Lotti was a Venetian composer of the Baroque period.

clue.text: Books about some retired theatre critic

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the word is read backwards
about means the books go round the other piece

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a group of books
any means some, as in have you any

explanation.surface: Volumes about a drama reviewer now out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the whole container backwards, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Tynan was a celebrated British drama reviewer for The Observer.

clue.text: She wrote of detecting or shaming a criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked, twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A crime writer exposes a felon or humiliates him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges ORSHAMINGA. Ngaio Marsh was a New Zealand writer of detective novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Ngaio Marsh wrote the Roderick Alleyn detective stories.

clue.text: Novelist's battle with a royal deserter

parts.note: Mons was a First World War battle
taken as written
R stands for royal, as in RN
a rat deserts, like rats leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A writer's war story about a royal who deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Monsarrat wrote The Cruel Sea.

clue.text: In Kenilworth, Amy steals paintings

parts.note: to steal is to rob
paintings are art

explanation.surface: In a Scott novel, a woman pinches pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy Robsart is the tragic heroine of Walter Scott's novel Kenilworth.

clue.text: East end joke overheard in Wren's masterpiece

indicators.note: overheard means the words are listened to rather than read

parts.note: Bow is a district in London's East End and a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A Cockney wisecrack is heard inside St Paul's, the architect's great work.
explanation.walkthrough: Wren is not Sir Christopher the architect but P.C. Wren, author of the Foreign Legion novel. Bow is in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau Geste is P.C. Wren's best-known novel, about brothers in the Foreign Legion.

clue.text: Child author, Daisy, remains cross

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
to ford a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: A young writer called Daisy is still annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains cross' reads as 'stays angry' but gives ASH and FORD. Daisy Ashford wrote The Young Visiters aged nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy Ashford wrote her novel The Young Visiters as a small girl.

clue.text: Article in a mess about Remembrance of Things Past

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about here means around and about, the letters scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammatical article is left in a muddle about Proust's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges only the letters of 'in a mess', which follow the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Anamnesis is recollection, the recalling to mind of what has gone before.

clue.text: Flower sown originally for Nancy and Peggy Blackett

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Amazon

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A bloom is planted for two girls in a children's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river. The Blackett sisters crew the dinghy Amazon in Arthur Ransome's Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy and Peggy Blackett call themselves pirates in Ransome's Swallows and Amazons, named after their boat.

clue.text: Male enters plus a fantastic river god

indicators.note: enters means the male goes into the other piece
fantastic means fanciful, the letters wildly rearranged

parts.note: he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man joins a wonderful deity of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' gives ALPUS from the letters of 'plus a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpheus is the river god of Greek myth who pursued the nymph Arethusa.

clue.text: A single key for Larkin's tomb?

parts.note: a single in cricket is one run
Del is the delete key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: One key could open the poet's grave.
explanation.walkthrough: Larkin's poem is An Arundel Tomb; the question mark is there because Arundel is not itself a word for tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin wrote the poem An Arundel Tomb, about a monument in Chichester Cathedral.

clue.text: In Paris the bishops use odd Woods' noted for architecture and illustration

definitions.text: Woods' noted for architecture and illustration

parts.note: le is French for the
B is bishop in chess notation, so two of them are BB

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters come out of order

explanation.surface: French bishops make strange use of a forest drawn by an architect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges USE into EUS. Lebbeus Woods was an American architect famous for visionary drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebbeus Woods was an American architect known for imaginative unbuilt designs shown in drawings.

clue.text: Play a chap who loved his work

definitions.meaning: the play by George Bernard Shaw about Eliza Doolittle

definitions.text: a chap who loved his work
definitions.meaning: the sculptor of Greek myth who fell in love with his own statue

explanation.definitionFit: Shaw named his play after the mythical Cypriot sculptor who fell for the statue he carved.

clue.text: Who took Cade's head is one to study

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a den is a study, a private room

explanation.surface: Someone takes off a rebel's head and settles down to read.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Henry VI Part 2, Alexander Iden kills the rebel Jack Cade and cuts off his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Iden is the Kentish gentleman who kills and beheads the rebel Jack Cade in Henry VI Part 2.

clue.text: British Lamb's placed before King David's brother

indicators.note: placed before means Lamb's name comes ahead of the British piece

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A British essayist's name sits ahead of a biblical king's sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote his Essays of Elia under that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliab was the eldest brother of David in the first book of Samuel.

clue.text: Thriller writer European locals embrace

indicators.note: embrace means the pubs hold the European piece within them

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub, an inn

explanation.surface: Pub regulars hug a writer from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locals' is British slang for the neighbourhood pub. Michael Innes wrote the Inspector Appleby mysteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Innes was the pen name of J.I.M. Stewart, who wrote mystery and suspense novels.

clue.text: What painters use, left out, softens

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is removed

parts.note: painters use easels to hold canvases

explanation.surface: Artists' stands, put aside, make things gentler.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking L out of EASELS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something is to lessen or soften it, as pain eases.

clue.text: One's left intensely worried about a sensation novel

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the letter A
worried means troubled, so the letters are agitated into a new order
left means the one has departed from the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is left anxious about a lurid Victorian thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes I from INTENSELY, leaving NTENSELY; 'worried' rearranges that, and 'about' wraps it round A. East Lynne was Mrs Henry Wood's Victorian bestseller.
explanation.definitionFit: East Lynne by Ellen Wood is a classic Victorian sensation novel of bigamy and secrets.

clue.text: Novelist of Middle Eastern extraction

indicators.note: extraction means letters are drawn out from inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A writer of Middle Eastern descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Middle Eastern extraction' looks like ancestry, but the letters are taken from the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Harper Lee and Laurie Lee were novelists; the name serves for either.

clue.text: Novel by male child of Noah

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard

explanation.surface: A book written by one of Noah's sons.
explanation.definitionFit: Shem was the eldest son of Noah in Genesis.

clue.text: Fools have succeeded in English society tests

parts.note: asses are fools
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Idiots have triumphed in exams for the English upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to evaluate or judge it.
